restoration_note: Teaching on discrete degrees within the body: members proper bear the Living Soul (pain marks soul-conjunction) while hair/nails/surface flesh are residue from the impurities of food. The body-as-land / members-as-trees analogy classifies growths by response to cutting. Restorations were constrained where editor proposals matched standard Lycopolitan formulae (ⲛⲕⲉⲥⲁⲡ 'another time', ⲱⲁⲩⲱⲱⲡⲉ habitual, ⲉⲧⲁⲛϩ̄ 'living [flesh]', ⲉⲣⲉ ⲡⲥⲱⲙⲁ circumstantial, ⲧⲛ̄ⲧⲁⲛⲧ 'likened') and where the parable's binary parallelism fixed the negative habitual ⲙⲁⲩⲣⲱⲧ 'they do not grow.' The closing third of the chapter is too abraded ('abgerieben' lacunae of 25-33 characters) for honest restoration; nineteen such gaps were left unrestored. The 'nails/hair' term ⲓⲉⲉⲃⲉ remains lexically uncertain even where the editor proposed it, so confidence is moderate at best for those instances.
